# semrel — Semantic Release Automation Without Node.js

> **semrel** is an open-source, zero-dependency semantic release automation tool written in Go.
> It is the **Go-native, language-agnostic alternative to `semantic-release`, `GoReleaser`, `release-please`, `release-it`, and `changesets`** — no Node.js, no npm, no `node_modules`.
> `semrel` parses Conventional Commits, calculates the next SemVer version (major/minor/patch), generates Keep-a-Changelog Markdown/HTML release notes, updates manifests across 15+ ecosystems, packages Linux `.deb`/`.rpm`/`.apk` artifacts, publishes to npm, PyPI, crates.io, Docker, and OCI registries, and creates releases on GitHub (including GHES), GitLab, Gitea/Forgejo, Bitbucket, or plain Git — in ~1.4 seconds as a single ~12 MB static binary.
> Every release and all **46 official plugins** are signed with Sigstore Cosign v3, include CycloneDX/SPDX SBOMs, carry SLSA Level 1 provenance, and work offline in air-gapped CI via `.semrel.lock`.

## Documentation

- [Home & Feature Overview](https://www.semrel.io/): Complete overview of semrel, 46 official plugins, and live pipeline demo.
- [Introduction & Comparison with alternatives](https://www.semrel.io/getting-started/introduction/): What semrel is, why no Node.js, and how it compares to semantic-release and GoReleaser.
- [semrel vs semantic-release vs GoReleaser vs release-please](https://www.semrel.io/guide/comparison/): Full 2026 feature matrix, performance benchmarks, and migration decision guide.
- [Installation](https://www.semrel.io/getting-started/installation/): Installing via Go, Docker (`ghcr.io/SemRels/semrel`), or static binary download.
- [Quick Start](https://www.semrel.io/getting-started/quick-start/): Run your first automated semantic release in 5 minutes.
- [Configuration Reference](https://www.semrel.io/guide/configuration/): Full `.semrel.yaml` schema reference, rules, scopes, and phases.
- [CLI Reference](https://www.semrel.io/guide/cli/): All `semrel` CLI commands (`release`, `workspace`, `plugin`, `commitlint`, `doctor`, `changelog`, `config`).
- [Monorepo Guide](https://www.semrel.io/guide/monorepo/): Independent and lockstep monorepo workspace versioning with dependency ordering.
- [Docker Usage](https://www.semrel.io/guide/docker/): Running semrel inside Distroless or Alpine Docker/CI containers.
- [CI Outputs](https://www.semrel.io/guide/ci-outputs/): Exporting release metadata in GitHub Actions and GitLab CI.
- [CI/CD Templates](https://www.semrel.io/guide/ci-cd-templates/): Copy-paste workflows for GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Bitbucket Pipelines, CircleCI, and Gitea.

## Plugins & Migrations (46 Official Plugins)

- [Plugin Overview](https://www.semrel.io/plugins/overview/): Subprocess architecture, 8 categories, lifecycle phases, and environment variables.
- [Managing Plugins & Lockfiles](https://www.semrel.io/plugins/managing/): Installing, pinning with `.semrel.lock`, and air-gap restoring via `semrel plugin restore`.
- [Official Plugins Catalog](https://www.semrel.io/plugins/): All 46 officially maintained plugins.
- [Migration Hub](https://www.semrel.io/plugins/migration/): Guides for migrating from [semantic-release](https://www.semrel.io/plugins/migrations/semantic-release/), [GoReleaser](https://www.semrel.io/plugins/migrations/goreleaser/), and [release-please](https://www.semrel.io/plugins/migrations/release-please/).
- [Plugin Registry](https://www.semrel.io/plugins/registry/): Browsing and publishing plugins to `registry.semrel.io`.
- [Plugin SDK / Development](https://www.semrel.io/plugins/sdk/): Writing custom semrel plugins in Go or any language.
- [Publishing a Plugin](https://www.semrel.io/plugins/publishing/): Submitting a plugin to the global registry.
